steps.title: Prepare complete DMEM medium
steps.instruction: Thaw frozen FBS and pen/strep in a 37 °C bead bath, then add 5.5 mL pen/strep and 50 mL FBS to 500 mL DMEM; invert to mix and store at 4 °C.

steps.title: Prepare 4 % PFA solution
steps.instruction: In a conical tube protected from light with aluminum foil, mix 3 mL of 16 % PFA with 9 mL PBS (total 12 mL); invert to mix, store at room temperature (up to 1 month) and handle with gloves in a fume hood.

steps.title: Prepare 0.1 % Triton X‑100 solution
steps.instruction: Add 400 µL Triton X‑100 to 400 mL PBS, stir, and store at room temperature (up to 1 month).

steps.title: Prepare 0.06 % Tween 20 solution
steps.instruction: Add 240 µL Tween 20 to 400 mL PBS, stir, and store at room temperature (up to 1 month).

steps.title: Prepare 2 % BSA solution
steps.instruction: Dissolve 500 mg BSA in 25 mL PBS, invert to mix, and store at 4 °C (up to 1 week).

steps.title: Plate cells on gridded dish
steps.instruction: Seed MEF WT NLS‑GFP in complete DMEM onto a single‑well gridded dish; incubate overnight at 37 °C, 5 % CO₂ to reach 50‑70 % confluency for time‑lapse imaging.

steps.title: Equilibrate microscope stage
steps.instruction: Set the microscope stage to 37 °C and 5 % CO₂ and allow it to equilibrate.

steps.title: Transfer and orient dish on microscope
steps.instruction: Move the gridded dish from the incubator to the microscope, ensure the grid is right‑side‑up under transmitted light, and mark the bottom of the dish for later orientation.

steps.title: Select fields of view
steps.instruction: Identify fields of view with ~70 % confluency, record their coordinates (e.g., A7, CS), choosing adjacent coordinates without overlapping cells.

steps.title: Run time‑lapse acquisition
steps.instruction: Perform the time‑lapse experiment using the standard imaging protocol; complete as quickly as possible to limit cell movement after acquisition.

steps.title: Replace medium with PBS
steps.instruction: After imaging, remove the dish from the microscope, return it to the hood, and replace the DMEM with 3 mL PBS.

steps.title: Fix cells with PFA
steps.instruction: In a fume hood, add 3 mL 4 % PFA to the dish, cover with foil, and incubate 15 min at room temperature; then discard PFA as hazardous waste.

steps.title: Wash fixed cells
steps.instruction: Remove PFA and wash the cells three times with 3 mL PBS for 5 min each; after the final wash, cells may be stored in 3 mL PBS at 4 °C (up to 1 month) wrapped in parafilm.

steps.title: Permeabilize with Triton X‑100
steps.instruction: Add 3 mL 0.1 % Triton X‑100 solution, incubate 15 min at room temperature, then remove.

steps.title: Treat with Tween 20
steps.instruction: Add 3 mL 0.06 % Tween 20 solution, incubate 5 min at room temperature, then remove.

steps.title: Wash after detergent steps
steps.instruction: Wash the cells three times with 3 mL PBS for 5 min each.

steps.title: Block with BSA
steps.instruction: Add 3 mL 2 % BSA solution, incubate 1 h at room temperature.

steps.title: Incubate primary antibody
steps.instruction: Remove BSA, add 1,000 µL primary antibody solution directly onto the cells (center of coverslip), wrap in parafilm, and incubate overnight at 4 °C.

steps.title: Wash after primary antibody
steps.instruction: Wash three times with 3 mL PBS for 5 min each.

steps.title: Incubate secondary antibody
steps.instruction: Add 1,000 µL secondary antibody solution directly onto the cells, place the dish on a nutating mixer for 1 h at room temperature.

steps.title: Wash after secondary antibody
steps.instruction: Wash three times with 3 mL PBS for 5 min each.

steps.title: Stain nuclei with Hoechst
steps.instruction: Add 1,000 µL Hoechst DNA stain directly onto the cells, incubate 15 min at room temperature.

steps.title: Final PBS rinse
steps.instruction: Wash three times with 3 mL PBS for 5 min each, then replace with 3 mL fresh PBS.

steps.title: Re‑orient dish for imaging
steps.instruction: Place the dish back on the microscope in the same orientation as during time‑lapse, using the previously drawn mark as a guide.

steps.title: Open time‑lapse reference images
steps.instruction: Load the time‑lapse image files, select the last frame of each recorded field of view as a visual reference.

steps.title: Locate matching coordinates
steps.instruction: In transmitted‑light mode, locate the recorded coordinates, adjust the stage until the cells match the last time‑lapse frame.

steps.title: Acquire immunofluorescence images
steps.instruction: Image each matching field of view using the standard fluorescence protocol; name each image to correspond to its time‑lapse counterpart.
